    @contextmanager
def set_ctx_var[T](var: ContextVar[T], value: T) -> Generator[T]:
    """Set a context variable within a context manager, restoring the previous value on exit.

    Args:
        var: The context variable to set.
        value: The value to set the context variable to.

    Returns:
        A context manager that yields the set value.
    """
    token = var.set(value)
    try:
        yield value
    finally:
        var.reset(token)

    def container_to_dict(
    container: Sequence | Set | Mapping | DataclassInstance | BaseModel,
    recursive: bool = True,
    _registry: dict[int, dict[Any, Any]] | None = None,
) -> dict[Any, Any] | None:
    """Turn an arbitrary container object into a dict.

    Args:
        container: The container to convert.
        recursive: Whether to recursively convert nested containers.
        _registry: Internal registry to track visited objects for cycle detection.

    Returns:
        A dict representation of the container, or None if not convertible.
    """
    _registry = _registry or {}

    obj_id = id(container)
    if obj_id in _registry:
        return _registry[obj_id]

    match container:
        case DataclassInstance():
            res = {
                Attr(f_name): getattr(container, f_name)
                for f_name in container.__dataclass_fields__.keys()
            }
        case _ if isinstance(container, BaseModel):
            res = {Attr(k): v for k, v in container.model_dump().items()}
        case Mapping():
            res = dict(container)
        case str() | bytes() | bytearray():
            # Scalars are iterable, but not containers to be indexed.
            return None
        case Iterable():
            res = {i: v for i, v in enumerate(container)}
        case _:
            return None

    _registry[obj_id] = res

    if recursive:
        for k, v in list(res.items()):
            m = container_to_dict(v, True, _registry)
            res[k] = m if m is not None else v

    return res

    def copy_and_override[**Params, DC: DataclassInstance](
    _init: Callable[Params, DC] | MaskedInit[Params, DC] | type[DC],
    _obj: DataclassInstance | tuple[DataclassInstance, ...],
    *args: Params.args,
    **kwargs: Params.kwargs,
) -> DC:
    """Re-construct a dataclass instance with all its init params + override.

    Args:
        _init: The dataclass constructor or a `MaskedInit` wrapping it.
        _obj: The dataclass instance(s) to copy values from.
        *args: Positional arguments to override.
        **kwargs: Keyword arguments to override.

    Returns:
        A new dataclass instance with the specified overrides.

    Note:
        Required attributes of the target dataclass type must always be provided as args / kwargs.

    Warning:
        Does not work for kw_only dataclasses and InitVars (yet).
    """
    if isinstance(_init, MaskedInit):
        _init = _init.constructor
    if not isinstance(_init, type):
        orig_init = get_origin(_init)
        assert orig_init is not None
        _init = orig_init

    constr_func = cast(Callable[..., DC], _init)
    target_fields = list(fields(cast(type, _init)))

    objs = _obj if isinstance(_obj, tuple) else (_obj,)

    obj_fields: dict[Field, Any] = {}
    for obj in objs:
        src_fields = set(f.name for f in obj.__dataclass_fields__.values())
        all_obj_fields = {f: getattr(obj, f.name) for f in target_fields if f.name in src_fields}
        obj_fields = {
            f: (
                v
                if v is not MISSING
                else obj_fields.get(
                    f,
                    (
                        f.default
                        if f.default is not MISSING
                        else (f.default_factory() if f.default_factory is not MISSING else MISSING)
                    ),
                )
            )
            for f, v in all_obj_fields.items()
        }

    assert not any(v is MISSING for v in obj_fields.values())

    obj_kwargs = list({f.name: v for f, v in obj_fields.items() if f.init}.items())
    new_kwargs = {
        **dict(obj_kwargs[len(args) :] if len(args) < len(obj_kwargs) else {}),
        **kwargs,
    }

    new_obj = constr_func(*args, **new_kwargs)  # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]

    for f, v in obj_fields.items():
        if not f.init:
            setattr(new_obj, f.name, v)

    return new_obj

    def flatten_dict(
    d: Mapping[Any, Any],
    path: tuple = (),
    _registry: dict[int, dict[tuple, Any]] | None = None,
) -> dict[tuple, Any]:
    """Turn a nested mapping into a flat dict (ignoring recursive references).

    Args:
        d: The mapping to flatten.
        path: The current path of keys (used for recursion).
        _registry: Internal registry to track visited objects for cycle detection.

    Returns:
        A flat dict mapping tuple paths to values.
    """
    items: dict[tuple, Any] = {}

    _registry = _registry or {}

    obj_id = id(d)
    if obj_id in _registry:
        return _registry[obj_id]

    _registry[obj_id] = items

    for k, v in d.items():
        new_path = path + (k,)
        if isinstance(v, Mapping):
            items.update(flatten_dict(v, new_path, _registry))
        else:
            items[new_path] = v

    return items

    def __init__(
    self,
    fget: AnyGetter[C, G] | None = None,
    cached: bool = False,
    mode: M | None = None,
    writable: bool = False,
    deletable: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Create a property descriptor."""
    self.__isabstractmethod__ = False

    self.fget = None
    self._name = None
    self.fset = None
    self.fdel = None
    self.mode = mode or "instance"  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
    self.cached = cached
    self.writable = writable
    self.deletable = deletable

    self._cls_cache_dict = {}
    self._instance_cache_dict = {}

    if fget is not None:
        self.getter(fget)

    def getter[C2, T2](self, fget: AnyGetter[C2, T2]) -> prop[C2, T2, M, W]:
    """Define the getter for this property."""
    assert self.fget is None, "Getter already defined"

    self.fget = fget  # type: ignore
    self._name = fget.__name__

    self.__module__ = fget.__module__
    self.__qualname__ = fget.__qualname__

    self.__name__ = fget.__name__

    return cast(prop[C2, T2, M, W], self)

    def cached_method[S, R, **P](
    func: Callable[Concatenate[S, P], R],
) -> Callable[Concatenate[S, P], R]:
    """Decorator to cache method results on the instance level."""

    @functools.wraps(func)
    def wrapper(self: S, *args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
        # ``vars`` is the receiver's own namespace, so a subclass never reuses a
        # cache an ancestor stored: inherited attributes would hide it from
        # ``hasattr`` and let classmethod caches leak down the MRO.
        cache_name = f"__{func.__name__}_cache"
        namespace = vars(self)
        if cache_name not in namespace:
            setattr(self, cache_name, {})

        # The function is part of the key: a decorated override and the decorated
        # base method it calls through ``super()`` share one cache attribute per
        # name, and without the function the override's result would be returned
        # for the base implementation too.
        cache: dict[tuple[Any, ...], R] = namespace[cache_name]
        key = (func, args, frozenset(kwargs.items()))

        if key not in cache:
            cache[key] = func(self, *args, **kwargs)

        return cache[key]

    return wrapper

    @cache
def get_distributions() -> dict[str, meta.Distribution]:
    """Get all installed Python package distributions."""
    metadata: dict[str, meta.Distribution] = {}

    for d in meta.distributions():
        try:
            metadata[d.metadata["Name"]] = d
        except meta.MetadataNotFound:  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
            continue

    return metadata

    def get_file_repo(path: Path) -> Repo | None:
    """Get the Git repository of given file, if any.

    Args:
        path: Path to the file.

    Returns:
        Git repository of the file, or ``None`` if not part of a Git repo.
    """
    try:

    except GitError:
        return None

    def get_module_distribution(module: ModuleType) -> meta.Distribution | None:
    """Get the distribution package of given module, if any.

    Args:
        module: Module to inspect.

    Returns:
        Distribution package of the module, or ``None`` if not part of a distribution.
    """
    mod_file = get_module_file(module)
    if mod_file is None:
        return None

    dists = {
        Path(str(dist.locate_file(f"{name}"))): dist for name, dist in get_distributions().items()
    }

    # An editable install resolves to the repository root, which contains the
    # whole virtual environment; the most specific (deepest) match wins so a
    # module in ``site-packages`` is attributed to its own distribution.
    mod_dists: list[tuple[int, meta.Distribution]] = []
    for dist_path, dist in dists.items():
        if mod_file.is_relative_to(dist_path):
            mod_dists.append((len(dist_path.parts), dist))
        elif dist.origin is not None and "url" in dist.origin.__dict__:  # type: ignore
            url = str(dist.origin.url)
            if url.startswith("file://"):
                path = _file_url_to_path(url)
                if mod_file.is_relative_to(path):
                    mod_dists.append((len(path.parts), dist))

    if len(mod_dists) == 0:
        return None

    return max(mod_dists, key=lambda item: item[0])[1]

    """Get the Git repository of given module, if any.

    Args:
        module: Module to inspect.

    Returns:
        Git repository of the module, or ``None`` if not part of a Git repo.

    def get_project_urls(dist: meta.Distribution, key: str) -> list[str]:
    """Get the documentation URL of given distribution, if any.

    Args:
        dist: Distribution to inspect.
        key: Key of the project URL to fetch.

    Returns:
        List of project URLs matching the given key.
    """
    if dist.metadata is None:
        return []

    proj_urls = dist.metadata.get_all("Project-URL")
    if proj_urls is None:
        return []

    proj_urls_split = [str(url).split(", ") for url in proj_urls]
    urls = [v for k, v in proj_urls_split if k == key]
    if len(urls) == 0:
        return []

    return urls

    @cache
def get_py_inventory(docs_url: str) -> Mapping[str, _InventoryItem]:
    """Return object inventory for given documentation URL.

    Args:
        docs_url: Documentation URL to fetch inventory from.

    Returns:
        Mapping of object names to inventory items.
    """
    inv_url = f"{docs_url.rstrip('/')}/objects.inv"

    res = requests.get(inv_url, allow_redirects=True)

    res.raise_for_status()

    inv_dict = inv.InventoryFile.load(
        BytesIO(res.content),  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
        docs_url,
        posixpath.join,
    )
    py_inv_dict = reduce(
        lambda a, b: {**a, **b},
        [v for k, v in inv_dict.items() if k.startswith("py:")],
        {},
    )

    return py_inv_dict

def open(self, mode: Literal["rw", "r", "w"] = "rw") -> Generator[I]:
    """Open the file and return its IO stream."""

    try:

    finally:

    @override
def __delitem__(self, key: str) -> None:
    """Delete an item from the directory."""
    self._ensure_exists()
    item_path = self.abs_path / key
    if item_path.is_file():
        item_path.unlink()
    elif item_path.is_dir():
        shutil.rmtree(item_path)
    else:
        raise KeyError(f"Item '{key}' not found in directory '{self.abs_path}'.")

    @override
def __getitem__(self, item: str) -> LocalDir | LocalFile:
    """Get an item from the directory."""
    self._ensure_exists()
    item_path = self.abs_path / item
    if item_path.is_dir():
        return LocalDir(path=item_path)
    elif item_path.is_file():
        return LocalFile.from_path(item_path)

    raise KeyError(f"Item '{item}' not found in directory '{self.abs_path}'.")

    @staticmethod
def from_path(path: Path | str) -> LocalFile:
    """Create a LocalFile from a given path."""
    path = Path(path).absolute()

    dir_path = path.parent
    name = path.stem
    # ``additional_mime`` covers the formats ``mimetypes`` cannot name
    # (parquet, npy, pickle, ...), so it takes precedence.
    mime = (
        additional_mime.get(path.suffix.lower())
        or guess_type(path)[0]
        or "application/octet-stream"
    )
    tags = tags_from_path(str(path)) if path.exists() else tags_from_filename(str(path))
    io_type = TextIO if "text" in tags else BinaryIO

    return LocalFile[cast(type[LiteralString], Literal[mime]), io_type, Any](
        dir=LocalDir(path=dir_path),
        name=name,
        _suffix=path.suffix,
    )

    def get_file_mode(
    self, mode: Literal["rw", "r", "w"], encoding: Literal["text", "binary"]
) -> str:
    """Map the file mode to a string representation."""
    if mode == "r":
        return "rb" if encoding == "binary" else "r"
    elif mode == "w":
        return "wb" if encoding == "binary" else "w"
    else:
        return "wb+" if encoding == "binary" else "w+"

    @override
def get_io(self, mode: Literal["rw", "r", "w"] = "rw") -> I:
    """Return the file's content as a text IO stream.

    Text streams always use UTF-8 with newline translation disabled, so the
    bytes on disk do not depend on the platform or locale and match what the
    serialization size estimators measure.
    """
    if is_subtype(self.io_type, TextIO):
        return cast(
            I,
            open(
                self.path,
                mode=self.get_file_mode(mode, "text"),
                encoding="utf-8",
                newline="",
            ),
        )

    return cast(I, open(self.path, mode=self.get_file_mode(mode, "binary")))

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
    """Normalize the content to the type implied by ``io_type``."""
    if self.content is None:
        self.content = "" if is_subtype(self.io_type, TextIO) else b""
    elif is_subtype(self.io_type, TextIO):
        if not isinstance(self.content, str):
            raise TypeError("A text file requires str content.")
    elif not isinstance(self.content, bytes):
        raise TypeError("A binary file requires bytes content.")

    @override
def get_io(self, mode: Literal["rw", "r", "w"] = "rw") -> I:
    """Return a stream over the file's content.

    Writes are stored back into :attr:`content` when the stream is closed.
    ``"w"`` and ``"rw"`` start from empty content, like a local file, while
    ``"r"`` starts from the current content and rejects writes.
    """
    initial = self.content if mode == "r" else None
    writable = mode != "r"

    if is_subtype(self.io_type, TextIO):
        return cast(
            I,
            _TextMemoryStream(
                self,
                cast(str, initial) if initial is not None else "",
                writable=writable,
            ),
        )

    return cast(
        I,
        _BinaryMemoryStream(
            self,
            cast(bytes, initial) if initial is not None else b"",
            writable=writable,
        ),
    )

    def ensure_dir_exists(path: Path | str) -> Path:
    """Make sure the given path exists and is a directory.

    Create dir if necessary. Then return the path unchanged.

    Args:
        path: Path to ensure exists.

    Returns:
        The given path.
    """
    path = Path(path).absolute()
    p = Path(path.parts[0])
    for d in path.parts[1:]:
        p = p / d
        if not p.is_dir():
            if not p.exists():
                p.mkdir()
            else:
                raise NotADirectoryError()

    return path

    @_hashing_context
def gen_int_hash(_ctx: set[int], obj: Any) -> int:  # noqa: C901
    """Generate stable hash for obj (must be known, hashable or composed of such).

    Args:
        obj: Object to hash.

    Returns:
        Hash of the object as integer.
    """
    match obj:
        case None:
            return 0
        case ModuleType():
            return gen_int_hash(obj.__name__)
        case type() | TypeAliasType():
            return gen_int_hash((obj.__module__, obj.__name__))
        case FunctionType() if hasattr(obj, "__name__"):
            return gen_int_hash(str(PyObjectRef.reference(obj).url))
        case FunctionType():
            # This may be unstable as closures are not considered.
            return gen_int_hash(list(obj.__code__.co_lines()))
        case GenericAlias() | UnionType():
            base = get_origin(obj)
            args = get_args(obj)
            return gen_int_hash(
                (
                    (
                        "types.UnionType"
                        if base is UnionType
                        else str(PyObjectRef.reference(base).url)
                    ),
                    *(gen_int_hash(arg) for arg in args),
                )
            )
        case Number() | str() | bytes() | date() | time() | datetime() | timedelta():
            return _stable_hash(obj)
        case tuple():
            return _hash_sequence(obj, _ctx)
        case _ if id(obj) in _ctx:
            return 0
        case _ if isinstance(obj, pd.DataFrame | pd.Series | pd.Index):
            # pandas types ``hash_pandas_object`` loosely, hence the ignore.
            return sum(hash_pandas_object(obj))  # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]
        case list():
            _ctx.add(id(obj))
            return _hash_sequence(obj, _ctx)
        case dict():
            _ctx.add(id(obj))
            return sum(_hash_sequence(item, _ctx) for item in obj.items())
        case set():
            _ctx.add(id(obj))
            return sum(gen_int_hash(item) for item in obj)
        case Hashable():
            _ctx.add(id(obj))
            return hash(obj)
        case DataclassInstance():
            _ctx.add(id(obj))
            return gen_int_hash({f.name: getattr(obj, f.name) for f in fields(obj)})
        # ``object`` has provided ``__getstate__`` since Python 3.11, so the
        # protocol alone matches every instance; require a custom state hook.
        case StatePicklable() if type(obj).__getstate__ is not object.__getstate__:
            state = obj.__getstate__()
            state = state if isinstance(state, tuple) else (state,)
            state_dicts = [s for s in state if isinstance(s, dict)]

            if len(state_dicts) == 0:
                raise ValueError()

            return sum(sum(_hash_sequence((k, v), _ctx) for k, v in s.items()) for s in state_dicts)
        case ArgsPicklable():
            args = obj.__getnewargs__()
            return sum(gen_int_hash(item) for item in args)
        case ArgsPicklableEx():
            args, kwargs = obj.__getnewargs_ex__()
            return sum(gen_int_hash(item) for item in args) + sum(
                gen_int_hash(item) for item in kwargs.items()
            )
        case _:
            if pl is not None:
                match obj:
                    case pl.DataFrame():
                        return sum(obj.hash_rows()) if not obj.is_empty() else 0
                    case pl.Series():
                        return sum(obj.hash())
                    case _:
                        pass

            raise ValueError()

    def gen_str_hash(x: Any, length: int = 10) -> str:
    """Generate stable hash for obj (must be known, hashable or composed of such).

    Args:
        x: Object to hash.
        length: Length of the returned hex string (zero-padded on the left).

    Returns:
        Hash of the object as a hex string.
    """
    s = hex(abs(gen_int_hash(x)))[2:]
    return s[:length].rjust(length, "0")

    @staticmethod
def from_url(url_text: str, obj_type: type[T]) -> "PyObjectRef[T]":
    """Create a reference from given URL.

    Args:
        url_text: URL text to parse.
        obj_type: Type of the referenced object.

    Returns:
        Reference to the object.
    """
    url = URL(url_text)

    repo_url = None
    if url.scheme.startswith("py+"):
        # Version and Python constraints are carried as query parameters,
        # so they must not leak into the repository URL.
        repo_url = str(
            URL.build(
                scheme=url.scheme[3:],
                host=url.host or "",
                port=url.port,
                path=url.path,
            )
        )

    if ":" not in url.fragment:
        raise ValueError(
            f"URL fragment must be of the form '<module>:<qualname>', got '{url.fragment}'."
        )

    module, object = url.fragment.split(":", 1)  # Split module and object

    return PyObjectRef(
        object_type=obj_type,
        repo_url=repo_url,
        version=url.query.get("version"),
        py_version=url.query.get("python"),
        module_name=module,
        qualname=object,
    )

    @staticmethod
def reference(  # noqa: C901
    obj: T2,
    version: str | None = None,
    version_strategy: VersionStrategy = "major",
) -> "PyObjectRef[T2]":
    """Create a reference to given object.

    Args:
        obj: Object to create reference for.
        version: Exact or range version specifier for the object's package/repo.
        version_strategy: Strategy to use for version range specification.

    Returns:
        Reference to the given object.
    """
    qualname = getattr(obj, "__qualname__", None)
    if qualname is None:
        raise ValueError("Object must have fully qualified name (`__qualname__`)")

    module = inspect.getmodule(obj)
    if module is None:
        raise ValueError("Object must be associated with a module.")

    dist = get_module_distribution(module)
    package = dist.name if dist is not None else None

    git_repo = None
    repo = None

    if dist is not None and dist.origin is not None:
        # Fetch the origin URL of the distribution, if any.
        repo = dict(dist.origin.__dict__).get("url")

    if dist is None or str(repo).startswith("file://"):
        # Not part of distribution or local file origin URL
        # -> assume first-party code commited to Git repo.
        git_repo = get_module_repo(module)
        if git_repo is not None:
            repo = git_repo.remote().url

    if repo is None:
        if dist is not None:
            # Code is part of distribution, but no explicit origin URL
            # -> assume PyPI indexed package
            repo = f"https://pypi.org/simple/{package}"
        elif module.__name__ != "builtins":
            # No distribution, no Git repo and not built-in module
            raise ValueError("Non-builtin object must be associated with a repository.")

    version_exact = None
    semver_exact = None

    if version is None:
        if dist is not None:
            version_exact = dist.version
            try:
                semver_exact = Version(version_exact)
            except InvalidVersion:
                pass
        elif git_repo is not None:
            current_tags = [tag for tag in git_repo.tags if tag.commit == git_repo.head.commit]
            if len(current_tags) > 0:
                for tag in current_tags:
                    version_exact = tag.name
                    try:
                        semver_exact = Version(version_exact)
                        break
                    except InvalidVersion:
                        continue
            elif not git_repo.head.is_detached:
                version_exact = git_repo.active_branch.name
                try:
                    semver_exact = Version(version_exact)
                except InvalidVersion:
                    pass

    if semver_exact is not None:
        version = version_to_range(semver_exact, version_strategy)
    elif version_strategy == "exact" and version_exact is not None:
        version = f"=={version_exact}"

    return PyObjectRef(
        object_type=type(obj),
        qualname=qualname,
        module_name=module.__name__,
        repo_url=repo,
        version=version,
        py_version=version_to_range(Version(f"{platform.python_version()}"), "minor"),
        _module=module,
        _dist=dist,
        _object=obj,
    )

    def get_all_module_dependencies(
    module: ModuleType,
    _ext_deps: set[str] | None = None,
    _int_deps: set[ModuleType] | None = None,
) -> tuple[set[str], set[ModuleType]]:
    """Return all (indirect) dependency modules of given module.

    Args:
        module: Module to inspect.

    Returns:
        Tuple of external and internal dependencies.
    """
    if _ext_deps is None:
        _ext_deps = set()
    if _int_deps is None:
        # Seed with the module itself so a dependency cycle does not report
        # the entry point as one of its own dependencies.
        _int_deps = {module}

    deps = [dep for _, m in inspect.getmembers(module) if (dep := inspect.getmodule(m)) is not None]
    ext_deps_map = {
        dep: dist.metadata["Name"]
        for dep in deps
        if (dist := get_module_distribution(dep)) is not None and dist.metadata is not None
    }
    new_ext_deps = set(ext_deps_map.values()) - _ext_deps

    these_int_deps = set(deps) - set(ext_deps_map.keys())
    new_int_deps = these_int_deps - _int_deps

    if len(new_ext_deps) > 0 or len(new_int_deps) > 0:
        _ext_deps |= new_ext_deps
        _int_deps |= new_int_deps

        for dependency in new_int_deps:
            sub_ext_deps, sub_int_deps = get_all_module_dependencies(
                dependency, _ext_deps, _int_deps
            )
            _ext_deps |= sub_ext_deps
            _int_deps |= sub_int_deps

        return _ext_deps, _int_deps - {module}

    return _ext_deps, _int_deps - {module}

    def get_outdated_deps(
    dist: meta.Distribution | ModuleType,
    allowed_diff: Specifier = Specifier("<=1.1.1"),
) -> dict[str, tuple[Version, Version]]:
    """Get a list of outdated dependencies of a distribution.

    Args:
        dist:
            Distribution to inspect.
            Can also be supplied as a module within the distribution in question.
        allowed_diff: Allowed difference between current and latest version.

    Returns:
        Dictionary of outdated package names with current and latest version.
    """
    if isinstance(dist, ModuleType):
        mod_dist = get_module_distribution(dist)
        if mod_dist is None:
            raise ValueError("Supplied module is not part of a distribution.")
        dist = mod_dist

    deps = get_dist_requirements(dist)

    if deps is None:
        return {}

    outdated = {}
    for dep in deps:
        try:
            dep_dist = meta.distribution(dep.name)
        except meta.PackageNotFoundError:
            dep_dist = dep.name

        versions = get_versions_on_pypi(dep_dist)
        versions = {
            v
            for v in versions
            if not v.is_prerelease and not v.is_postrelease and not v.is_devrelease
        }

        matching_req = set(dep.specifier.filter(versions))
        newest_matching = max(matching_req)

        newer = versions - matching_req
        if len(newer) == 0:
            continue

        newest = max(newer)
        diff = version_diff(newest, newest_matching)
        if diff is not None and diff not in allowed_diff:
            outdated[dep.name] = (newest_matching, newest)

    return outdated

    def get_versions_on_pypi(package: meta.Distribution | str) -> set[Version]:
    """Get all available versions of given distribution.

    Args:
        package: Distribution or package name to inspect.

    Returns:
        Set of available versions.
    """
    if isinstance(package, meta.Distribution):
        if package.origin is not None:
            return set()
        package = package.name

    url = f"https://pypi.org/pypi/{package}/json"

    response = requests.get(url)
    if response.status_code == 404:
        return set()

    data = response.json()

    versions = set()
    for v in data["releases"].keys():
        try:
            versions.add(Version(v))
        except InvalidVersion:
            pass

    return versions

    def semver_range_to_spec(semver_range: str) -> SpecifierSet:
    """Convert semver range to Python version specifier.

    Args:
        semver_range: Semver range string.

    Returns:
        Corresponding Python version specifier set.
    """
    match = re.match(r"^(?P<op>\^|~|>=|<=|==|=|>|<)?(?P<version>.+)$", semver_range.strip())
    if match is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid semver range: '{semver_range}'.")

    op = match.group("op")
    version = Version(match.group("version").strip())

    if op == "^":
        return SpecifierSet(f">={version.public},<{version.major + 1}")

    if op == "~":
        return SpecifierSet(f">={version.public},<{version.major}.{version.minor + 1}")

    if op in (">=", "<=", ">", "<"):
        return SpecifierSet(f"{op}{version.public}")

    return SpecifierSet(f"=={version.public}")

    def version_diff(v1: Version, v2: Version) -> Version | None:
    """Get the difference between two versions (v1 - v2).

    Args:
        v1: Newer version.
        v2: Older version.

    Returns:
        Difference between ``v1`` and ``v2`` as Version, or ``None`` if ``v1 < v2``
    """
    if v1 < v2:
        return None

    v1_arr = (v1.major, v1.minor, v1.micro)
    v2_arr = (v2.major, v2.minor, v2.micro)

    diff = tuple(a - b for a, b in zip(v1_arr, v2_arr))

    if diff[0] > 0:
        diff = (diff[0], v1_arr[1], v1_arr[2])
    elif diff[1] > 0:
        diff = (diff[0], diff[1], v1_arr[2])

    return Version(".".join(str(v) for v in diff))

    def version_to_range(version: Version, strategy: VersionStrategy = "major") -> str:
    """Convert exact version to version range.

    Args:
        version: Exact version to convert.
        strategy: Version strategy to use.

    Returns:
        Version range string.
    """
    return (
        f"=={version}"
        if strategy == "exact"
        else f"~{version}"
        if strategy == "minor"
        else f"^{version}"
    )

    def get_full_args_dict(
    func: Callable, args: Sequence, kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return dict of all args + kwargs.

    Args:
        func: Function to inspect.
        args: Positional arguments given to the function.
        kwargs: Keyword arguments given to the function.

    Returns:
        Dictionary of all args + kwargs.
    """
    argspec = inspect.getfullargspec(func)

    posonlyargs = list(getattr(argspec, "posonlyargs", ()))
    posarg_names = [*posonlyargs, *argspec.args]

    arg_defaults = argspec.defaults or []
    defaulted_names = posarg_names[len(posarg_names) - len(arg_defaults) :]
    defaults = dict(zip(defaulted_names, arg_defaults))
    defaults |= dict(argspec.kwonlydefaults or {})

    # Handle bound methods
    if len(posarg_names) > 0 and posarg_names[0] == "self" and hasattr(func, "__self__"):
        posarg_names = posarg_names[1:]

    posargs = dict(zip(posarg_names[: len(args)], args))

    return {**defaults, **posargs, **(kwargs or {})}

    def get_subclasses[T](cls: type[T], max_level: int | None = None, _level: int = 1) -> list[type[T]]:
    """Return all subclasses of given class.

    Args:
        cls: The class to get subclasses for.
        max_level: Maximum inheritance level to traverse.
        _level: Current inheritance level (for internal use).

    Returns:
        List of subclasses.
    """
    if max_level is not None and _level > max_level:
        return []

    subclasses = list(dict.fromkeys(cls.__subclasses__()))

    for subclass in cls.__subclasses__():
        for sub_subclass in get_subclasses(subclass, max_level=max_level, _level=_level + 1):
            if sub_subclass not in subclasses:
                subclasses.append(sub_subclass)

    return subclasses

    @staticmethod
def match(
    targets: Iterable[SerializationTarget[Any, Any, Any]],
    types: Collection[TypeDef[Serialized]] | None = None,
    scope: TransportScope | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
) -> list[SerializationTarget[T, S, L]]:
    """Return the subset of targets that match any of the given types.

    Args:
        targets: The list of serialization targets to filter.
        types: The collection of types to match against.
        scope: The scope to match.
        lossless: Whether to only include lossless targets.

    Returns:
        The list of matching serialization targets.
    """
    return cast(
        list[SerializationTarget[T, S, L]],
        [
            t
            for t in targets
            if (
                any((TypeRef(tt).is_subtype_of(t.type)) for tt in types)
                if types is not None
                else True
            )
            and (_scope_serves(t.scope, scope) if scope is not None else True)
            and (not lossless or t.lossless)
        ],
    )

    def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: V,
    target_type: TypeDef[T] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: S = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[V] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Estimate the byte size of serializing ``instance`` to ``target_type``.

    Drivers override this when they can measure their format cheaply. The
    default falls back to :func:`sys.getsizeof`, which measures the object
    in memory rather than the encoded representation.

    Args:
        instance: The object to be serialized.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        The estimated number of bytes.
    """
    return sys.getsizeof(instance)

    @classmethod
def lossless_target(cls, hint: TypeDef[Any]) -> bool:
    """Whether a target format round-trips the object exactly.

    A file target does exactly when all of its MIME types are declared
    lossless by the serializer; a target that is not a file follows
    :attr:`__lossless_values__`.

    Args:
        hint: The target type to check.

    Returns:
        ``True`` if the target is lossless for this serializer.
    """
    mimes = target_mimes(hint)

    return (
        all(mime in cls.__lossless_mimes__ for mime in mimes)
        if mimes
        else cls.__lossless_values__
    )

    @prop(cached=True, mode="class")
def serialization_targets(self) -> list[SerializationTarget[T, S, Any]]:
    """Serialization targets supported by this serializer, as declared in its type arguments."""
    typeref = self._typeref.typevar_map[T]
    # The declarations are the driver's: the requested scope of an operation
    # is applied to the target when it is dispatched, so this metadata only
    # states what the serializer itself can serve.
    declared = self.scopes
    return cast(
        list[SerializationTarget[T, S, Any]],
        [
            SerializationTarget(type=member, scope=scope, lossless=self.lossless_target(member))
            for member in typeref.members
            for scope in declared
        ],
    )

    The declaration is the receiver and the requests are the arguments: a declaration serves a request when the request is an instance of the declared scope, so a serializer declared for :class:Open serves every request, while one declared for a narrower scope cannot serve an unrestricted one.     def match(self, scopes: Collection[TransportScope | type[TransportScope]]) -> bool:
    """Check whether this declared scope can serve any of the requested scopes.

    The declaration is the receiver and the requests are the arguments: a
    declaration serves a request when the request is an instance of the
    declared scope, so a serializer declared for :class:`Open` serves every
    request, while one declared for a narrower scope cannot serve an
    unrestricted one. Scopes form a hierarchy rooted at :class:`Open`, and
    the comparison is the class relation, never an exact-class match.

    Args:
        scopes: The requested scopes, as classes or values.

    Returns:
        ``True`` if this declaration can serve at least one request.
    """
    return any(_scope_serves(self, scope) for scope in scopes)

              click based_datatypes.serialize.UnsupportedTargetError href "" "based_datatypes.serialize.UnsupportedTargetError"

    A serializer cannot produce the requested target.

    A driver raises this when the requested format cannot carry what it was asked to write — a JSON or YAML file cannot hold a file produced for a nested item, for example. :func:serialize and :func:estimate_serialized_size treat it as a selection miss: they try the next matching serializer and only raise when none can fulfil the target.

    def deserialize[V2](
    source: Serialized,
    annotation: TypeDef[V2],
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
) -> V2:
    """Deserialize an object from the source type or format.

    Args:
        source: The source object to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.

    Returns:
        An instance of the object, deserialized from the source.
    """
    # Reading is not restricted to lossless formats: the lossiness of a format
    # describes what an export can drop, not what an import can restore.
    candidates = get_serializers(
        annotation,
        targets=[_source_type(source)],
        scope=scope,
        lossless=False,
    )

    if len(candidates) == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No suitable serializer found for {type(source).__name__} as "
            f"{annotation!r} under scope {scope!r}."
        )

    _, _, driver = candidates[0]

    if isinstance(driver, type) and issubclass(driver, Serializable):
        return cast(
            V2,
            driver.__deserialize__(
                source,
                scope=scope,
                realm=realm,
                annotation=cast(TypeDef[Serializable[Any, Any]], annotation),
            ),
        )
    else:
        return cast(V2, driver.deserialize(source, scope=scope, realm=realm, annotation=annotation))

    def estimate_serialized_size[T2: Serialized](
    instance: Any,
    target_type: TypeDef[T2],
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Serializable[T2]] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Estimate the byte size of serializing ``instance`` to ``target_type``.

    Serializers override this when they can measure their format cheaply. The
    default falls back to :func:`sys.getsizeof`, which measures the object
    in memory rather than the encoded representation.

    Args:
        instance: The object to be serialized.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The estimated number of bytes.
    """
    candidates = get_serializers(
        typ=annotation if annotation is not None else type(instance),
        targets=[target_type] if target_type is not None else None,
        scope=scope,
        lossless=lossless,
        value=instance if annotation is None else None,
    )

    if len(candidates) == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No suitable serializer found for {type(instance).__name__} to "
            f"{target_type!r} under scope {scope!r} "
            f"with lossless={lossless}."
        )

    return _dispatch(
        candidates,
        lambda driver, target: (
            driver.__estimate_serialized_size__(
                instance,
                target_type=target_type,
                lossless=target.lossless,
                scope=scope,
                annotation=annotation,
            )
            if isinstance(driver, type)
            else driver.estimate_serialized_size(
                instance,
                target_type=target_type,
                lossless=target.lossless,
                scope=scope,
                annotation=annotation,
            )
        ),
        scope,
        realm,
    )

    def get_serializers[U, T: Serialized, S: TransportScope, L: bool](
    typ: TypeDef[U],
    targets: Collection[TypeDef[T]] | None = None,
    scope: S = Open(),
    lossless: L = False,
    value: object | None = None,
) -> list[tuple[int, SerializationTarget[T, S, L], Serializer[U, T, S] | type[Serializable[T, S]]]]:
    """Get the serializers that can handle a given type or instance.

    Args:
        typ: The type or instance to get the serializer for.
        targets: The serialization targets to write to or read from. Instances are
            matched on their MIME type and IO type, so the serializer for the actual
            format wins; types only narrow by class. ``None`` skips the target
            check and returns the serializers for the object type alone.
        scope: The scope to select for. A serializer declared for a supertype
            scope (e.g. Open) also serves a request for a narrower one.
        lossless: When ``True``, only serializers that round-trip the target
            format without loss are eligible; ``False`` accepts either.
        value: The instance to select for. A type alone cannot express element
            constraints — an SQL statement list and ``[1, 2]`` are both ``list`` —
            so a value is validated against the driver's declared object type as
            well. ``None`` matches on the type only, which is what introspection
            wants.

    Returns:
        A list of tuples of the form ``(index, target, driver)``, where
        ``index`` is the index of the matching target in the list of targets,
        ``target`` is the matching serialization target and ``driver`` is the
        serializer or serializable class to handle the object.
    """
    candidates = []

    cls = TypeRef(typ).common_type

    if issubclass(cls, Serializable):
        candidates = sorted(
            [
                (i, t, cls)
                for i, t in enumerate(
                    SerializationTarget.match(
                        cls.__serialization_targets__(), targets, scope, lossless
                    )
                )
            ],
            key=lambda x: x[0],
        )  # Sort by index to prioritize the first match

    if len(candidates) > 0:
        return candidates  # pyright: ignore[reportReturnType]

    candidates = sorted(
        [
            (i, t, driver)
            for driver in custom_serializers + common_serializers
            if _handles(driver, typ, value)
            for i, t in enumerate(
                SerializationTarget.match(driver.serialization_targets, targets, scope, lossless)
            )
        ],
        key=lambda x: x[0],
    )  # Sort by index to prioritize the first match

    return candidates  # pyright: ignore[reportReturnType]

    def read_structure(path: Path | str) -> SerializedDict:
    """Read a local directory tree back into a serialized dictionary.

    Primitive values come from ``__index__.yaml``, files are returned as
    :class:`LocalFile` handles, and sub-directories are read recursively.

    Args:
        path: The directory to read.

    Returns:
        The serialized dictionary stored in the directory.
    """
    structure = _read_node(Path(path).absolute())

    if not isinstance(structure, dict):
        raise TypeError(f"{path} holds a list, not a dictionary.")

    return structure

    @contextmanager
def serialization_context(
    target: SerializationTarget[Any, Any, Any], realm: Realm | None = None
) -> Generator[None]:
    """Context manager to set the current serialization context."""
    token = current_ser_ctx.set((target, realm))
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        current_ser_ctx.reset(token)

    def serialize[T2: Serialized](
    instance: Any,
    target_type: TypeDef[T2] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Serializable[T2]] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> T2:
    """Serialize an object to the target type or format.

    When no target type is given, the serializer picks its preferred format: the
    first one it declares, which is the lossless one wherever it has a choice.
    ``lossless`` therefore only filters the selection once a target is requested.

    Args:
        instance: The object to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The serialized target object.
    """
    candidates = get_serializers(
        typ=annotation if annotation is not None else type(instance),
        targets=[target_type] if target_type is not None else None,
        scope=scope,
        # Without a requested target the driver picks its preferred format, so
        # there is no format to judge: the lossless filter applies only once a
        # target is asked for.
        lossless=lossless if target_type is not None else False,
        # With no annotation the instance itself narrows the selection: a bare
        # ``list`` cannot say whether it holds SQL statements or integers.
        value=instance if annotation is None else None,
    )

    if len(candidates) == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No suitable serializer found for {type(instance).__name__} to "
            f"{target_type!r} under scope {scope!r} "
            f"with lossless={lossless}."
        )

    return cast(
        T2,
        _dispatch(
            candidates,
            lambda driver, target: (
                driver.__serialize__(
                    instance,
                    target_type=target_type if target_type is not None else target.type,
                    lossless=target.lossless,
                    scope=scope,
                    realm=realm,
                    file_factory=file_factory,
                    annotation=annotation,
                )
                if isinstance(driver, type)
                else driver.serialize(
                    instance,
                    target_type=target_type if target_type is not None else target.type,
                    lossless=target.lossless,
                    scope=scope,
                    realm=realm,
                    file_factory=file_factory,
                    annotation=annotation,
                )
            ),
            scope,
            realm,
        ),
    )

    write_structure ¤

    write_structure(
    structure: SerializedDict, path: Path | str
) -> LocalDir

    Write a serialized dictionary into a local directory tree.

    The directory is created when it does not exist. Entries are overwritten by key, and an entry whose key changes shape (a file replaced by a sub-directory, or the other way round) replaces the old artifact instead of being overlaid on it. Entries that the structure no longer mentions at all are left in place, so writing an updated structure over an existing tree does not delete anything.

    def write_structure(structure: SerializedDict, path: Path | str) -> LocalDir:
    """Write a serialized dictionary into a local directory tree.

    The directory is created when it does not exist. Entries are overwritten by
    key, and an entry whose key changes shape (a file replaced by a
    sub-directory, or the other way round) replaces the old artifact instead of
    being overlaid on it. Entries that the structure no longer mentions at all
    are left in place, so writing an updated structure over an existing tree
    does not delete anything.

    Args:
        structure: The serialized dictionary to write.
        path: The directory to write into.

    Returns:
        The directory that was written.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a key is not a valid entry name, or would take the name of
            the directory index.
    """
    directory = ensure_dir_exists(path)
    _write_node(structure, directory)

    return LocalDir(path=directory)

    @staticmethod
def match(
    targets: Iterable[SerializationTarget[Any, Any, Any]],
    types: Collection[TypeDef[Serialized]] | None = None,
    scope: TransportScope | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
) -> list[SerializationTarget[T, S, L]]:
    """Return the subset of targets that match any of the given types.

    Args:
        targets: The list of serialization targets to filter.
        types: The collection of types to match against.
        scope: The scope to match.
        lossless: Whether to only include lossless targets.

    Returns:
        The list of matching serialization targets.
    """
    return cast(
        list[SerializationTarget[T, S, L]],
        [
            t
            for t in targets
            if (
                any((TypeRef(tt).is_subtype_of(t.type)) for tt in types)
                if types is not None
                else True
            )
            and (_scope_serves(t.scope, scope) if scope is not None else True)
            and (not lossless or t.lossless)
        ],
    )

    self,

    @classmethod
def lossless_target(cls, hint: TypeDef[Any]) -> bool:
    """Whether a target format round-trips the object exactly.

    A file target does exactly when all of its MIME types are declared
    lossless by the serializer; a target that is not a file follows
    :attr:`__lossless_values__`.

    Args:
        hint: The target type to check.

    Returns:
        ``True`` if the target is lossless for this serializer.
    """
    mimes = target_mimes(hint)

    return (
        all(mime in cls.__lossless_mimes__ for mime in mimes)
        if mimes
        else cls.__lossless_values__
    )

    @prop(cached=True, mode="class")
def serialization_targets(self) -> list[SerializationTarget[T, S, Any]]:
    """Serialization targets supported by this serializer, as declared in its type arguments."""
    typeref = self._typeref.typevar_map[T]
    # The declarations are the driver's: the requested scope of an operation
    # is applied to the target when it is dispatched, so this metadata only
    # states what the serializer itself can serve.
    declared = self.scopes
    return cast(
        list[SerializationTarget[T, S, Any]],
        [
            SerializationTarget(type=member, scope=scope, lossless=self.lossless_target(member))
            for member in typeref.members
            for scope in declared
        ],
    )

    Check whether this declared scope can serve any of the requested scopes.

    The declaration is the receiver and the requests are the arguments: a declaration serves a request when the request is an instance of the declared scope, so a serializer declared for :class:Open serves every request, while one declared for a narrower scope cannot serve an unrestricted one. Scopes form a hierarchy rooted at :class:Open, and the comparison is the class relation, never an exact-class match.

    def match(self, scopes: Collection[TransportScope | type[TransportScope]]) -> bool:
    """Check whether this declared scope can serve any of the requested scopes.

    The declaration is the receiver and the requests are the arguments: a
    declaration serves a request when the request is an instance of the
    declared scope, so a serializer declared for :class:`Open` serves every
    request, while one declared for a narrower scope cannot serve an
    unrestricted one. Scopes form a hierarchy rooted at :class:`Open`, and
    the comparison is the class relation, never an exact-class match.

    Args:
        scopes: The requested scopes, as classes or values.

    Returns:
        ``True`` if this declaration can serve at least one request.
    """
    return any(_scope_serves(self, scope) for scope in scopes)

              click based_datatypes.serialize.base.UnsupportedTargetError href "" "based_datatypes.serialize.base.UnsupportedTargetError"

    A serializer cannot produce the requested target.

    A driver raises this when the requested format cannot carry what it was asked to write — a JSON or YAML file cannot hold a file produced for a nested item, for example. :func:serialize and :func:estimate_serialized_size treat it as a selection miss: they try the next matching serializer and only raise when none can fulfil the target.

    @contextmanager
def serialization_context(
    target: SerializationTarget[Any, Any, Any], realm: Realm | None = None
) -> Generator[None]:
    """Context manager to set the current serialization context."""
    token = current_ser_ctx.set((target, realm))
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        current_ser_ctx.reset(token)

    def target_mimes(hint: Any) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return the MIME types a file target declares.

    Args:
        hint: A target type, a :class:`TypeRef`, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The declared MIME types, in declaration order; empty when the hint is not
        a file target.
    """
    if hint is None:
        return ()

    ref = hint if isinstance(hint, TypeRef) else TypeRef(hint)

    for var, value in ref.typevar_map.items():
        if var == M:
            return cast(tuple[str, ...], tuple(value.literal_values))

    return ()

Without a requested target type the first declared format is used, and a file format is delivered as an in-memory :class:MemoryFile.

    Serializer for mappings, sequences, sets and dataclass instances.

    Every item is serialized on its own, so a container of datetimes, UUIDs, dataclasses or further containers becomes JSON-shaped data as long as each item can be serialized; an item that serializes to a file is nested in the payload as that file, which is what a directory tree stores. All containers reduce to a dictionary or a list, so this driver only declares those value targets — writing JSON or YAML files stays with :class:JSONSerializer.

    @override
def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: Container,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Measure the encoded container.

    The payload is built first, because translating nested items is part of
    the cost; the encoded size is then measured with the C-level JSON encoder.
    """
    payload = _container_payload(instance, scope, None)
    mimes = target_mimes(target_type)

    return _json_estimate(payload, mimes[0] if len(mimes) > 0 else "application/json")

    @override
def serialize(
    self,
    instance: Container,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> SerializedDict | list[SerializedValue]:
    """Serialize a container to the JSON-shaped payload it reduces to.

    Args:
        instance: The container to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: Unused; this serializer produces values, not files.

    Returns:
        The dictionary or list the container reduces to.

    Raises:
        UnsupportedTargetError: If a file target is requested, which this driver
            does not produce.
    """
    if file_factory is not None or _is_file_hint(target_type):
        raise UnsupportedTargetError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} reduces a container to a value, not to a file; "
            "serialize the payload to a file target through its own serializer."
        )

    return cast(
        SerializedDict | list[SerializedValue],
        _container_payload(instance, scope, realm),
    )

    Structural marker that matches every dataclass instance.

    A dataclass shares no method that a protocol could key on, so the marker uses the class hook instead of inheritance: any class carrying __dataclass_fields__ counts as a subclass.

    @classmethod
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type) -> bool:
    """Treat every dataclass as a subclass of this marker."""
    if cls is DataclassValue:
        return hasattr(subclass, "__dataclass_fields__")

    return NotImplemented

    @override
def serialize(
    self,
    instance: BeautifulSoup,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> str | HTMLFile:
    """Serialize a soup to HTML text or to an HTML file.

    Args:
        instance: The soup to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The written file, or the HTML text when a text target was requested.
    """
    text = str(instance)
    target = self._resolve_target(target_type, file_factory)

    if target is None:
        return text

    _write_text(target, text)

    return target

    @override
def deserialize(
    self,
    source: ImageFile,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> Image.Image:
    """Deserialize an image from an image file.

    Args:
        source: The file to deserialize from.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        The deserialized image.
    """
    file = _require_file(source, type(self).__name__)

    with file.open("r") as stream:
        image = Image.open(stream)
        image.load()

    return check_type_and_cast(image, annotation)

    @override
def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: Image.Image,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Estimate the uncompressed pixel payload.

    Container overhead and compression are not modelled, so the result
    can be smaller than a tiny compressed file.
    """
    bytes_per_band = _BYTES_PER_BAND.get(instance.mode, 1)

    return int(instance.width * instance.height * len(instance.getbands()) * bytes_per_band)

    @override
def serialize(
    self,
    instance: Image.Image,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> ImageFile:
    """Serialize an image to an image file.

    Args:
        instance: The image to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The written file.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the target MIME type is not supported.
    """
    target = self._file_target(target_type, file_factory)

    # The encoder comes from the target format, never from the source
    # image: a JPEG loaded from disk must still be written as PNG when
    # the target is a PNG, or the payload contradicts the declared loss.
    image_format = _image_format_for_mime(target.default_mime)
    if image_format is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported image MIME type: {target.default_mime}")

    with target.open("w") as stream:
        instance.save(stream, format=image_format)

    return target

    @override
def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: JSONDict,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Measure the encoded dictionary.

    The JSON encoder is C, so measuring costs less than any Python size walk
    of the same data; a YAML target is measured from the compact JSON payload
    instead, because the YAML dumper is pure Python and far slower.
    """
    mimes = target_mimes(target_type)

    return _json_estimate(instance, mimes[0] if len(mimes) > 0 else "application/json")

    self,

    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,

    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,

) -> SerializedDict | JSONFile:
    """Serialize a dictionary to a JSON or YAML file, or return it as it is.

    Args:
        instance: The dictionary to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The written file, or the dictionary when a dict target was requested.
    """
    target = self._resolve_target(target_type, file_factory)

    if target is None:
        return cast(SerializedDict, instance)

    _write_text(target, _serialize_json(instance, target.default_mime))

    return target

    @override
def deserialize(
    self,
    source: NpFile,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Deserialize an array from ``.npy``, ``.npz`` or CSV.

    Args:
        source: The file to deserialize from.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        The deserialized array.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the source MIME type is not supported.
    """
    file = _require_file(source, type(self).__name__)

    with file.open("r") as stream:
        if file.default_mime == "application/x-npy":
            array = np.load(cast(BinaryIO, stream), allow_pickle=False)
        elif file.default_mime == "application/x-npz":
            array = np.load(cast(BinaryIO, stream), allow_pickle=False)["arr_0"]
        elif file.default_mime == "text/csv":
            array = np.loadtxt(cast(TextIO, stream), delimiter=",")
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MIME type: {file.default_mime}")

    return check_type_and_cast(array, annotation)

    @override
def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: np.ndarray,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Estimate the encoded size from the array's memory footprint."""
    if target_mimes(target_type)[:1] in (
        ("application/x-npy",),
        ("application/x-npz",),
    ):
        _require_native_dtype(instance)

    if target_mimes(target_type)[:1] == ("application/x-npy",):
        # The ``.npy`` format prepends a fixed 128-byte header.
        return instance.nbytes + 128

    return instance.nbytes

    @override
def serialize(
    self,
    instance: np.ndarray,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> NpFile:
    """Serialize an array to ``.npy``, ``.npz`` or CSV.

    Args:
        instance: The array to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The written file.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the target MIME type is not supported.
        TypeError: If the array holds Python objects.
    """
    target = self._file_target(target_type, file_factory)
    mime = target.default_mime

    # Both checks run before the target is opened, so a rejected array or
    # format cannot truncate an existing file.
    if mime not in {"application/x-npy", "application/x-npz", "text/csv"}:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MIME type: {mime}")

    if mime in {"application/x-npy", "application/x-npz"}:
        _require_native_dtype(instance)

    with target.open("w") as stream:
        if mime == "application/x-npy":
            np.save(cast(BinaryIO, stream), instance)
        elif mime == "application/x-npz":
            np.savez(cast(BinaryIO, stream), arr_0=instance)
        else:
            np.savetxt(cast(TextIO, stream), instance, delimiter=",")

    return target

    @override
def deserialize(
    self,
    source: DfFile,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Deserialize a DataFrame from Parquet, Excel or CSV.

    Args:
        source: The file to deserialize from.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        The deserialized frame.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the source MIME type is not supported.
    """
    file = _require_file(source, type(self).__name__)

    with file.open("r") as stream:
        if file.default_mime == "text/csv":
            frame = pd.read_csv(stream)
        elif file.default_mime == "application/vnd.apache.parquet":
            frame = pd.read_parquet(cast(BinaryIO, stream))
        elif file.default_mime == "application/vnd.ms-excel":
            frame = pd.read_excel(cast(BinaryIO, stream))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MIME type: {file.default_mime}")

    return check_type_and_cast(frame, annotation)

    @override
def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: pd.DataFrame,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Estimate the encoded size, sampling CSV output by row."""
    if target_mimes(target_type)[:1] == ("text/csv",):
        total = len(instance)
        if total == 0:
            return 0

        sample = instance.iloc[:: _sample_step(total)]
        return int(_encoded_size(sample.to_csv(index=False)) * total / len(sample))

    return int(instance.memory_usage(deep=True).sum())

    @override
def serialize(
    self,
    instance: pd.DataFrame,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> DfFile:
    """Serialize a DataFrame to Parquet, Excel or CSV.

    Args:
        instance: The frame to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The written file.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the target MIME type is not supported.
    """
    target = self._file_target(target_type, file_factory)
    mime = target.default_mime

    # The format is checked before the target is opened, so a rejected
    # format cannot truncate an existing file.
    if mime not in {
        "text/csv",
        "application/vnd.apache.parquet",
        "application/vnd.ms-excel",
    }:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MIME type: {mime}")

    with target.open("w") as stream:
        if mime == "text/csv":
            instance.to_csv(stream, index=False)
        elif mime == "application/vnd.apache.parquet":
            instance.to_parquet(cast(BinaryIO, stream))
        else:
            instance.to_excel(cast(BinaryIO, stream), index=False)

    return target

def deserialize(
    self,
    source: PickleFile,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """Deserialize any object from a Pickle file.

    Args:
        source: The file to deserialize from.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        The deserialized object.
    """
    file = _require_file(source, type(self).__name__)

    with file.open("r") as stream:
        obj = pickle.load(stream)  # noqa: S301

    return check_type_and_cast(obj, annotation)

    @override
def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: Any,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Measure the pickle payload without writing it.

    The pickler is C and about eighty times faster than summing
    :func:`sys.getsizeof` over the object graph in Python, and no cheaper proxy
    bounds the payload, which depends on the pickler's own opcode stream.
    """
    return len(pickle.dumps(instance))

def serialize(
    self,
    instance: Any,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> PickleFile:
    """Serialize any object to a Pickle file.

    Args:
        instance: The object to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

        The written file.
    """
    target = self._file_target(target_type, file_factory)

    with target.open("w") as stream:
        pickle.dump(instance, cast(BinaryIO, stream))

    return target

    @override
def deserialize(
    self,
    source: DfFile,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Deserialize a DataFrame from Parquet, Excel or CSV.

    Args:
        source: The file to deserialize from.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        The deserialized frame.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the source MIME type is not supported.
    """
    file = _require_file(source, type(self).__name__)

    with file.open("r") as stream:
        if file.default_mime == "text/csv":
            frame = pl.read_csv(stream)
        elif file.default_mime == "application/vnd.apache.parquet":
            frame = pl.read_parquet(cast(BinaryIO, stream))
        elif file.default_mime == "application/vnd.ms-excel":
            frame = pl.read_excel(cast(BinaryIO, stream))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MIME type: {file.default_mime}")

    return check_type_and_cast(frame, annotation)

    @override
def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: pl.DataFrame,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Estimate the encoded size, sampling CSV output by row."""
    if target_mimes(target_type)[:1] == ("text/csv",):
        total = instance.height
        if total == 0:
            return 0

        sample = instance.gather_every(_sample_step(total))
        return int(_encoded_size(sample.write_csv()) * total / sample.height)

    return int(instance.estimated_size())

def deserialize(
    self,
    source: T,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> V:
    """Deserialize an object from a JSON-supported value.

    Args:
        source: The value to deserialize from.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        An instance of the object, deserialized from the value.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the source is a file.
    """
    if isinstance(source, File):
        raise TypeError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} deserializes from a JSON value, "
            f"got a {type(source).__name__}."
        )

    return check_type_and_cast(self._decode(source, annotation), annotation)

        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: Unused; these serializers never write files.

    Returns:
        The serialized value.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a file target is requested.
    """
    if file_factory is not None or _is_file_hint(target_type):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} serializes to a JSON value, not to a file; embed "
            "the value in a dict or list to write it to a file."
        )

    return self._encode(instance)

    @override
def deserialize(
    self,
    source: SerializedDict | JSONFile,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> pyd.BaseModel:
    """Deserialize a model from a JSON or YAML file, or from its dump.

    Args:
        source: The file or dictionary to deserialize from.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The model type to validate against.

    Returns:
        The deserialized model.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no annotation is given.
    """
    if annotation is None:
        raise ValueError("Deserializing a Pydantic model requires the model as annotation.")

    return pyd.TypeAdapter(annotation).validate_python(_read_value(source))

    @override
def estimate_serialized_size(
    self,
    instance: pyd.BaseModel,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Measure the serialized model without writing it.

    The JSON-mode dump is unavoidable — it is what the model's fields mean
    once serialized — but it is a C-level pass, and the payload is then
    measured the same way as a plain dictionary.
    """
    mimes = target_mimes(target_type)

    return _json_estimate(
        instance.model_dump(mode="json"),
        mimes[0] if len(mimes) > 0 else "application/json",
    )

    @override
def serialize(
    self,
    instance: pyd.BaseModel,
    target_type: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    lossless: bool = True,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    file_factory: Callable[[], File] | None = None,
) -> SerializedDict | JSONFile:
    """Serialize a model to a JSON or YAML file, or return its dump.

    ``mode="json"`` converts dates, UUIDs and decimals to JSON-native
    values, so a value the encoder rejects cannot truncate an existing
    file and YAML's safe dumper accepts it. Aliases and excluded fields
    do not survive the dump, which is why the format is not lossless.

    Args:
        instance: The model to serialize.
        target_type: The target type or format to serialize to.
        lossless: Whether to require a lossless serialization.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the serialization.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.
        realm: The realm to serialize to.
        file_factory: An optional factory function to create new files.

    Returns:
        The written file, or the model dump when a dict target was requested.
    """
    dump = cast(SerializedDict, instance.model_dump(mode="json"))
    target = self._resolve_target(target_type, file_factory)

    if target is None:
        return dump

    _write_text(target, _serialize_json(dump, target.default_mime))

    return target

    @override
def deserialize(
    self,
    source: str | SQLFile,
    scope: TransportScope = Open(),
    realm: Realm | None = None,
    annotation: TypeDef[Any] | None = None,
) -> SQLStatement:
    """Deserialize statements from SQL text or from an SQL file.

    Args:
        source: The file or text to deserialize from.
        scope: The serialization scope to use for the deserialization.
        realm: The realm to deserialize from.
        annotation: The declared type of the object, if any.

    Returns:
        The deserialized statements.
    """
    statements = [sqla.text(str(stmt)) for stmt in sqlparse.parse(_read_text(source))]

    # Rebuild the container the annotation asks for; the statement count
    # alone cannot tell a scalar from a one-element list.
    origin = get_origin(annotation)
    shaped: object
    if origin is list or origin is Sequence:
        shaped = statements
    elif origin is tuple:
        shaped = tuple(statements)
    elif len(statements) == 1:
        shaped = statements[0]
    else:
        shaped = statements

    return check_type_and_cast(shaped, annotation)
